spans.s:
ātura-saṁnyāsa
(‘saṁnyāsa taken by one who is afflicted’)
------------------------------------------
Saṁnyāsa or monastic life is the last of the four āśramas or stages of life through which every द्विज (‘the twice-born’) has to pass. Generally every pious द्विज entertains the desire of dying as a saṁnyāsin, since that enhances his chance of मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन् which is the ultimate goal of human life.
Life being uncertain, situations may so arise in life that a man may die without taking सṁन्यास. For such persons afflic-ted with mortal diseases or facing grave dangers, the धर्मशास्त्रस् have provided an emergency ritual by which they can take सṁन्यास and hence die as saṁnyāsins. This is called ‘ātura-सṁन्यास.’
The essentials of this ritual are: सङ्कल्प (resolve to take सṁन्यास), kṣaura (tonsure of the head), सावित्री-praveśa (merging the गायत्री मन्त्र into प्रणव or Om) and praiṣoccāra (uttering the praiṣamantra, signifying renunciation).
Even among these, the first and the last are enough if there is no scope for performing the other aspects of the ritual.
If by chance, a person who has taken āturasaṁnyāsa survives the ordeal, he is expected to take regular सṁन्यास with all the formalities. He cannot go back to the old way of life.
See also SAṀNYĀSA.
